# SOP-P1-L4-02 Product changeover - Heat Treat line
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P1, line P1-L4
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03
Related documents: MM-P1-L4-HT03, QS-PROC-05, SOP-P1-L4-05

Purpose
1. Describe the standardized steps for product changeover on the Heat Treat line to minimize downtime, ensure process integrity, and maintain traceability. This procedure applies to all operators and technicians responsible for EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

Scope and background
2. Changeovers on the Heat Treat line require coordinated mechanical, thermal, and tooling adjustments. The objective is to switch from one product family to another with documented checks and handoffs. Rationale: consistent changeover practice reduces scrap, prevents cross-contamination, and maintains heat-treat cycle integrity. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for maintenance-specific tasks, QS-PROC-05 for quality record requirements, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for upstream material preparation steps.

Preconditions (required before starting)
3. Verify the following before initiating changeover:
   - Production schedule authorizes the changeover and the new job number is available.
   - All incoming material is staged and verified per SOP-P1-L4-05.
   - Any open non-conformances related to the Heat Treat line are addressed or documented per QS-PROC-05.
   - Maintenance clearance for mechanical interventions is obtained if required (see MM-P1-L4-HT03).

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE for changeover activities:
   - Heat-resistant gloves for handling components from EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
   - Safety glasses with side shields.
   - Hearing protection when within the active load/unload zone of EQ-P1-L4-HP02.
   - Cut-resistant gloves for tooling adjustment at EQ-P1-L4-CN01.

Changeover steps (numbered)
5. Stop current production and secure area
   5.1. Notify downstream and upstream operators that changeover is starting.
   5.2. Place lockout/tagout per site protocol if any mechanical maintenance is required (see MM-P1-L4-HT03).
   5.3. Record stop time and reason in the shift log required by QS-PROC-05.

6. Clean and clear process path
   6.1. Remove residual parts from EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.
   6.2. Wipe down contact surfaces and tooling nests to remove debris. Keep cleaning records as per QS-PROC-05.

7. Inspect and prepare tooling and fixtures
   7.1. Confirm tooling required for the new product is available and tagged for this job.
   7.2. Fit check new tooling on EQ-P1-L4-CN01 and inspect for wear. Document findings in equipment log.
   7.3. Lubrication: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is CFW-LUB-477. Apply lubrication following the lubrication schedule in MM-P1-L4-HT03 and log application.

8. Machine setup and warm-up
   8.1. Load new program and verify program ID matches job sheet.
   8.2. Perform dry-run or air-cycle to verify motion and clearance; record anomalies.
   8.3. Spindle warm-up: For EQ-P1-L4-CN01 allow spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes prior to cutting. Use the spindle-warm log to record start and end of warm-up.

9. Process parameter verification
   9.1. Confirm heat-treat cycle selection at EQ-P1-L4-HT03 is as specified for new product. If a thermal profile change is required, consult MM-P1-L4-HT03 for maintenance input.
   9.2. Verify conveyor and transfer timing at EQ-P1-L4-HP02 to ensure consistent load rates.
   9.3. Document all parameter confirmations on the changeover checklist.

10. Trial run and first-piece inspection
   10.1. Produce a defined number of trial pieces as indicated on the job sheet.
   10.2. Inspect first-piece measurements and features, comparing to the job print and QS-PROC-05 sampling requirements.
   10.3. If trial pieces meet acceptance, sign off to proceed to production. If not, document deviations and escalate to engineering.

11. Bring line back to production
   11.1. Gradually ramp load rates and monitor process stability.
   11.2. Maintain heightened inspection frequency for the first production batch as required by QS-PROC-05.
   11.3. Record start of production and job number in the production log.

Examples and rationale
12. Example: When switching from a short-run part to a long-run part, the spindle warm-up time prevents early dimensional drift during the first cuts. The specified spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes to stabilize bearing temperatures and reduce runout. Using the correct lubricant (CFW-LUB-477) helps maintain consistent spindle performance across changeovers. These steps minimize rework and ensure heat-treat cycles apply to parts within specification.

Records to keep
13. Maintain the following records per QS-PROC-05:
   - Changeover checklist with timestamps.
   - Lubrication application entry specifying the use of CFW-LUB-477.
   - Spindle warm-up log showing the 15 minutes warm-up period for EQ-P1-L4-CN01.
   - First-piece inspection reports and any NCRs.
   - Any maintenance or adjustments recorded per MM-P1-L4-HT03.

Escalation and hold points
14. Hold production and contact engineering if:
   - First-piece inspection fails to meet acceptance criteria.
   - Any abnormal noise, vibration, or thermal readings persist following warm-up and trial run.
   - Tooling mismatches or fixture damage is detected.

Sign-off (required)
15. The following sign-offs are required to close a changeover:
   - Operator signature confirming completion of steps 5 through 11 and records attached.
   - Supervisor signature confirming review of records and first-piece acceptance.
   - Maintenance signature if any MM-P1-L4-HT03 interventions were performed.

Change history
16. Revision history maintained in document control.

Related documents
17. Refer to MM-P1-L4-HT03 for maintenance tasks and lubrication schedules, QS-PROC-05 for quality and records requirements, and SOP-P1-L4-05 for upstream material preparation.
